# VRFLogStore

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Logging` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Logger/VRFLogStore.cs#L19)

Collects every framework log line whether or not the window is open, so opening the Logger
shows what already happened instead of starting blank.
Kept as a ScriptableSingleton backed by a file in Library: Unity re-serializes it around a
domain reload, which is what lets the buffer survive entering play mode and recompiling.

```csharp
[FilePath("Library/VRFrameworkLogger.dat", FilePathAttribute.Location.ProjectFolder)]
public class VRFLogStore : ScriptableSingleton<VRFLogStore>
```

### Clear() {#clear}

Empties the buffer and resets every count. Rows still in the Unity Console are not brought
back; only what it logs from now on shows up.

```csharp
public void Clear()
```

[View source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Logger/VRFLogStore.cs#L505)

### ClearWithConsole() {#clearwithconsole}

The Logger's Clear: empties the buffer and the Unity Console with it. A compile error
survives the Console's clear, so while the Console is mirrored, what it kept is read back
in and both still show the same lines.

```csharp
public void ClearWithConsole()
```

[View source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Logger/VRFLogStore.cs#L525)
